title: Coarse-Grained Boltzmann Generators
claim: A two-branch learned pipeline, with a potential model and a generative proposal trained in parallel, yields exactly reweighted samples at reduced dimensionality.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, parallel top/bottom branches, reweighting equation in final panel
description: Three numbered panels read left to right. Panel 1, Coarse-Graining & Data Generation, shows a solvated peptide in a cloud of faint water molecules. An arrow labeled Ξ(r) maps it to a small coarse-grained chain. Below is a double-well free-energy curve with an Enhanced Sampling arrow, captioned Biased/Unbiased Trajectories. Panel 2, Parallel Learning, has two stacked boxes. The top blue box holds a PMF network icon with Force Matching, and an arrow leads to a blue 3D energy surface labeled U_η(R). The bottom grey box holds a normalizing flow network icon with Flow Matching, and an arrow leads to a grey surface labeled q_θ(R). Panel 3, Asymptotically Exact Sampling, centers on the reweighting formula ω(R) ∝ exp(−βU_η(R))/q_θ(R). Generated molecule samples feed the formula. It outputs the target equilibrium distribution p(R), drawn as a bimodal curve with unbiased estimates. Blue marks the PMF path and grey marks the flow path.
caption: CG-BG framework. Atomistic configurations are mapped to CG coordinates to construct training data. A PMF network learns $U_\eta(R)$ from rapidly converged data, while a normalizing flow learns a proposal density $q_\theta(R)$ over CG configurations. Samples generated from the flow are reweighted using the PMF to recover the target equilibrium distribution $p(R)$, enabling unbiased estimation of thermodynamic observables.
abstract: Sampling equilibrium molecular configurations from the Boltzmann distribution is a longstanding challenge. Boltzmann Generators (BGs) address this by combining exact-likelihood generative models with importance sampling, but practical scalability is limited. Meanwhile, coarse-grained surrogates enable the modeling of larger systems by reducing effective dimensionality, yet often lack a reweighting procedure required to ensure asymptotically correct statistics. In this work, we propose Coarse-Grained Boltzmann Generators (CG-BGs), a framework for reduced-order generative modeling with importance sampling in coarse-grained coordinate space. CG-BGs generate samples using a flow-based model and reweight them using a learned potential of mean force (PMF). We show that the PMF can be learned from rapidly converged trajectories via enhanced sampling force matching. Experiments demonstrate that CG-BGs capture solvent-mediated interactions in highly reduced representations while substantially reducing computational cost relative to atomistic BGs, providing a practical route toward equilibrium sampling of larger molecular systems.
